newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - Bears rule roost in SE Asian markets.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Bears rule roost in SE Asian markets.

text.p: Rubber prices in Southeast Asia will continue to languish in the doldrums because of poor demand and ample supplies, traders said on Monday.
"I see the continuation of the bear market," a senior dealer at a Western commodity trading company in Singapore told Reuters. "There's still too much rubber while demand remains thin."
"This is quite a bad time for rubber sellers," a dealer in the west Sumatran city of Padang in Indonesia said "Demand continues to be weak."

The only thing that might perk up prices would be the spot September expiry in Japan on Tuesday, especially if a Japanese firm that had taken a long position decided to take large deliveries to protect its position, traders said.
"But any rally will be short-lived. The fundamentals of the market remains bearish," a Singapore-based trader said.
Those fundamentals include weak buying from major consumers in the West and rising rubber stocks in Japan, dealers said.
In Indonesia, the benchmark tyre-grade SIR20 prices will probably remain soft this week, but sentiment on latex may firm up on talk of lower supply in Medan, dealers said.

SIR20 offer prices for October/November shipments were likely to remain stable in the range between 56.00-56.50 U.S. cents/lb fob Medan, 55.75-56.25 cents fob Palembang, Surabaya and Padang, and at 55.00-57.00 cents fob Jambi and Pontianak.
Sentiment on latex was likely to firm up in the coming week following the loading of some 2,000 tonnes in Medan, a dealer said.

"I heard they are currently loading some 2,000 tonnes of latex to the U.S. This piece of positive news is likely to boost sentiment a bit," the dealer said, adding the deal was signed at 2,335 rupiah/kg several months ago.
High amoniac grade latex prices were last traded at 2,240 rupiah/kg in Medan and at 2,230 rupiah/kg in the western Javanese cities of Bandung and Tangerang, dealers said.
The Medan-based dealer said he sold SIR3CV at 150 U.S. cents/kg recently, but added that prices were likely to fall as state-owned plantations were making offers at around 137 cents/kg.
In Thailand, nearby rubber prices were steady to lower this week in a quiet market and the mood will not likely lift, industry sources said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for October shipment was quoted around US$1.26-1.29 this week, compared with $1.28-1.29/kg last week.
Latex price was also steady at $1.02/kg, they said.
There were only few enquiries and high Japanese stocks continued to pressure the market, they said.
The actual amount of Thai rubber entering the market this week is not expected to be much different from the previous week when about 287,000 kg of rubber got into the market.
In Malaysia, sluggish overseas demand and increasing domestic supply will drag down Malaysian rubber prices this week, dealers said.
"The Europeans should be back and buying actively as the summer holidays have ended and with factories resuming their operations," a dealer at a broking firm said.
"They should need the raw materials but they are not seen in the market yet," the dealer added.
Traders expect European buyers to come in to make fresh enquiries for SMR CV, SMR L, SMR 10 and some latex grades of rubber for prompt shipment.
Buying from Asian consumers, particularly China, has slowed down, dealers said.
"Producers are quoting at higher levels but buyers are mostly sidelined," one trader said. Buyers speculated prices may fall because of a fresh influx of supplies into the market, he added.
"The supplies are slowly coming back as rains have stopped in some rubber growing areas in Malaysia," the dealer said.
Dealers are offering SMR CV at Malaysian 375-377 cents a kg, SMR L at 354-356 cents, SMR 10 at 313-315 cents and drum latex at 245-250 cents.
The Malaysian benchmark October RSS1 was quoted on Friday at 324.50 cents a kg against 329 cents a week ago, and October SMR 20 at 313 cents against 314 cents.
(With contributions from Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur and Jakarta)
- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
